title: Printed but not benchmarkable: most building-decarbonisation disclosure cannot be matched to the pathways that stranding regulation assumes
abstract: arXiv:2607.22006v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Cities are beginning to enforce carbon limits on existing buildings. Science-based decarbonisation pathways set those limits one asset type and one jurisdiction at a time. Owners, however, report for the whole firm. We measure what that mismatch costs on two sets of public corporate reports: a census of 502 reports from the 119 listed built-environment firms with a collected report inside a 2,246-firm panel (2003-2023), and 519 real-estate reports from 101 firms (2007-2024). BeDA, a multimodal language-model tool whose reliability we test first, read them. Running the pathway frameworks' own entry tests over published disclosure: 16.5% of census reports (43.7% of real-estate reports) print an operational carbon intensity per square metre; 6.6% (25.0%) can be matched to a pathway for their property type in a covered jurisdiction; and only 5.0% (16.4%) disclose the floor area they divided by. translated_title: 已披露却无法对标：大多数建筑脱碳信息披露无法与搁浅监管所假设的脱碳路径相匹配
translated_abstract: 城市开始对既有建筑实施碳排放限制。基于科学的脱碳路径一次针对一种资产类型和一个司法管辖区来设定这些限制，然而业主却以整个公司为单位进行报告。我们在两组公开的企业报告上衡量了这种错配的代价：一组是对2,246家公司面板（2003-2023年）中拥有已收集报告的119家上市建筑环境公司共502份报告的普查；另一组是来自101家公司的519份房地产报告（2007-2024年）。这些报告由BeDA——一个多模态语言模型工具，其可靠性经我们先行测试——进行阅读。在公开披露上运行路径框架自身的准入测试后发现：16.5%的普查报告（房地产报告中为43.7%）印有每平方米运营碳强度；6.6%（25.0%）能够与其资产类型在覆盖司法管辖区内的路径相匹配；而只有5.0%（16.4%）披露了计算时所除以的建筑面积。在路径测试中失败的……
tldr: 该研究利用多模态语言模型工具BeDA分析了1000余份企业公开报告，发现仅有5.0%的建筑环境公司报告（房地产报告为16.4%）披露了与科学脱碳路径匹配所必需的建筑面积数据，揭示了企业碳披露体系与建筑搁浅监管假设之间的严重脱节。
en_tdlr: Using the multimodal language-model tool BeDA to analyze over 1,000 corporate reports, this study finds that only 5.0% of built-environment firm disclosures (16.4% of real-estate reports) provide the floor-area data required to match science-based building-decarbonisation pathways, exposing a fundamental mismatch between corporate carbon disclosure and the assumptions of stranding regulation.
